studies.officialTitle: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Phase 3 Trial to Compare the Efficacy and Safety of HRS9531 and Placebo in Subjects With Overweight or Obese

design.description: Four-arm 1:1:1:1 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial evaluating once-weekly subcutaneous injections of HRS9531 at 2 mg, 4 mg, and 6 mg versus placebo for 48 weeks across clinical sites in China.

studies.population: Chinese adults aged 18 years or older with obesity (BMI >= 28 kg/m2) or overweight (BMI >= 24 kg/m2) with at least one weight-related comorbidity, without diabetes.
studies.safetySummary: Most treatment-emergent adverse events were mild to moderate and gastrointestinal-related. Permanent treatment discontinuation rates due to TEAEs were very low: 0.7% (2 mg), 0.7% (4 mg), 1.4% (6 mg), and 0% (placebo).

studies.officialTitle: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Phase 2 Clinical Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of HRS9531 Tablets in Obese Subjects

design.description: Four-arm 1:1:1:1 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial of once-daily oral ribupatide tablets at 10 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg versus placebo for 26 weeks in adults living with obesity without diabetes.

studies.population: Chinese adults aged 18 to 65 years with obesity (BMI >= 28 kg/m2) and without type 2 diabetes.
studies.safetySummary: Most treatment-emergent adverse events were mild to moderate and gastrointestinal. Rates of vomiting were 2.4% (10 mg), 11.4% (25 mg), and 7.5% (50 mg); rates of nausea were 11.9% (10 mg), 22.7% (25 mg), and 20.0% (50 mg). No permanent treatment discontinuations or down-titrations due to nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or constipation were reported.

studies.safetySummary: Ribupatide was well-tolerated with a favorable safety profile; most TEAEs were mild and gastrointestinal-related.
